message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait/efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is explicitly prevalent but still aligned). Among them, PGS003972/PGS003973 come from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet 2023) with broad multi-cohort development, which domain_knowledge suggests should generally outrank pan-trait/portability framework scores (PGS001784; PGS002054) and an older sparse P+T score (PGS000753), absent clearly stronger PRS-comparable metrics. Between PGS003972 and PGS003973, both share the same method (PRS-CS), variant count, and European evaluation; however PGS003973’s very high reported C-index (0.882) is a full-model metric and cannot be treated as PRS-only, and its covariates (Age, Age^2, Sex) may contribute strongly, so it is not decisive. PGS003972 has similarly basic/unknown covariates and reports a more modest full-model AUROC (0.69), but the key advantage is the same disease-focused study family without relying on an outlier covariate-driven discrimination claim. Overall evidence supports selecting the Nat Genet disease-meta-analysis family, but confidence is limited because PRS-only AUROC/incremental AUROC are not provided for these top candidates and several competitors have large validations with modest PRS-only R2/partial-r, making the ranking not fully resolved from comparable metrics."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are abdominal aortic aneurysm variants). However, several come from framework/portability-style efforts (PGS001784: Global Biobank framework; PGS002054: UKB portability paper) and one is a sparse older P+T score (PGS000753, 29 variants), which domain guidance suggests down-ranking versus disease-focused multi-cohort meta-analysis scores when available. PGS003972 (Nat Genet AAA meta-analysis; PRS-CS; broad multi-cohort development; EUR evaluation) offers the strongest disease-focused evidence package among the listed options and reports a full-model AUROC=0.69; its sibling model PGS003973 reports a higher C-index (0.882) but with covariates Age/Age^2/Sex and without any PRS-only or covariates-regressed-out metric, making the discrimination less comparable and potentially more covariate-driven per the provided policy. Confidence is not high because none of the disease-focused candidates provide clearly isolated PRS-only AUROC/R2, and the highest reported discrimination metrics are full-model/covariate-including, limiting clean cross-candidate comparison."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003973","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (abdominal aortic aneurysm or prevalent AAA). Among them, PGS003972 and PGS003973 come from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet) with multi-cohort development, which domain_knowledge indicates should generally outrank pan-trait/portability framework scores (e.g., PGS001784 from Global Biobank analyses; PGS002054 from a UKB portability study) when endpoints are similarly aligned. Between the two Nat Genet scores, PGS003973 has the stronger reported discrimination metric in its selected European validation record (C-index 0.882 with CI 0.872–0.892; n=7,517) versus PGS003972 (AUROC 0.69; n=6,940), and its covariates (Age, Age^2, Sex) are basic and comparable. However, confidence is not high because most candidates lack PRS-only AUROC/R2, and the very high full-model C-index for PGS003973 could be substantially covariate-driven (consistent with the local heritability sanity-check guidance), with no incremental/PGS-only metrics provided to isolate PRS contribution."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (AAA diagnosis; one is explicitly prevalent). Two candidates (PGS002054, PGS001784) come from pan-trait/framework papers (UKB portability; Global Biobank analyses), which domain_knowledge advises down-ranking when disease-focused alternatives exist. The most disease-focused option with clean/basic covariates and a directly interpretable PRS effect size is PGS000753 (Circulation; AAA genetics in MVP; covariates age/sex/PCs; OR per SD 1.37 [1.30–1.44]), providing PRS-specific signal without relying on full-model AUROC. Competing disease-focused recent scores (PGS003972/PGS003973, Nat Genet AAA meta-analysis) report only full-model discrimination (AUROC/C-index) with limited PRS-isolated metrics and one has only moderate full-model AUROC (0.69), while the other’s high C-index (0.882) is not directly comparable as a PRS-only metric and could be largely covariate-driven; PGS003429 is tied to a screening cost-effectiveness context and also reports only full-model AUROC. Overall, PGS000753 is preferred on disease-focused context plus PRS-specific effect-size evidence, but confidence is limited because no candidate provides clearly comparable PRS-only AUROC/incremental metrics across models and several newer disease-focused options exist with large multi-cohort development but incomplete PRS-isolated reporting in the provided metadata."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait/EFO and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (abdominal aortic aneurysm or prevalent AAA). Two candidates (PGS001784, PGS002054) come from pan-trait/framework-style papers (“Global Biobank…”, “Portability of 245 polygenic scores…”) and are down-ranked per domain_knowledge when disease-focused alternatives exist, despite having large validation and modest PRS-comparable metrics (PGS001784 pgs-only R2=0.014661; PGS002054 partial-r=0.0144). Three newer disease-focused candidates exist (PGS003429/PGS003972/PGS003973), but their reported discrimination is primarily full-model AUROC/C-index (0.69–0.882) with PGS-only metrics absent and covariates partly unknown, making cross-model PRS contribution hard to compare; the heritability guidance also cautions against treating high full-model AUROC as PRS evidence when PGS-only metrics are missing. PGS000753 is selected as the best-supported direct-match because it comes from an AAA-focused study (“Genetic Architecture of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm…”) with clean basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), explicit effect-size evidence (OR per SD=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) and multi-ancestry evaluation including EUR, while avoiding the framework-paper penalty. Outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because key comparable PRS metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2) are missing or non-uniform across the disease-focused set, and one high full-model C-index (PGS003973) cannot be interpreted as PRS-only contribution from the visible metadata."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm; PGS000753 is explicitly prevalent AAA but still aligned). The strongest disease-focused, multi-cohort development appears to be the Nat Genet AAA GWAS meta-analysis models (PGS003972/PGS003973), with broad AAA-relevant contributing cohorts and European evaluation; among them, PGS003972 is supported by the cleanest/basic covariate set (covariates listed as unknown rather than a potentially more restrictive specification) and a reported full-model AUROC of 0.69, while avoiding reliance on very high full-model metrics. Competing options have notable limitations: PGS001784 and PGS002054 come from pan-trait/framework portability papers (Cell Genom ‘Global Biobank…’ and AJHG ‘Portability of 245…’), making them less preferred when a disease-focused alternative exists despite their large validation and small PRS-side R2/partial-r; PGS003429 is from a screening cost-effectiveness context with only full-model AUROC (0.708) and unknown covariates; PGS000753 is older, very sparse (29 variants) and reports only an OR. Overall confidence is limited because most candidates lack clearly comparable PRS-only discrimination (PGS-only AUROC/incremental AUROC are absent), and several reported high full-model AUROCs (e.g., 0.868/0.882) are not directly interpretable as PRS performance per the provided domain policy."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo align to abdominal aortic aneurysm; phenotyping_reported is AAA diagnosis, with PGS000753 specifically prevalent AAA). Among the non-framework, disease-focused options, PGS003972/PGS003973 come from a dedicated AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet 2023) with multi-cohort development, which domain guidance suggests should usually outrank pan-trait/framework or portability sweeps when endpoint alignment is comparable. Between the two Nat Genet scores, PGS003972 is preferred because its reported discrimination is less likely to be dominated by covariates: it reports AUROC=0.69 with covariates unknown, whereas PGS003973 reports a very high C-index=0.882 but includes age/age^2/sex (which can strongly drive full-model discrimination in AAA) and does not provide an isolated PRS-only metric, making that headline C-index less interpretable for PRS contribution. The main limitation is that PRS-only AUROC/R2 and incremental metrics are largely missing across candidates, and covariates are unknown for PGS003972, so confidence cannot be high."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004606","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_efo (age-related macular degeneration), but they vary in endpoint fidelity and evidence quality.
